_schema_notes.purpose: Reference dataset of LLM SDK request-entry functions. STPA treats matching calls as black-box nodes in the PAG: taint flows from inputs to outputs by a summary rule (Item 2) instead of descending into the callee.
_schema_notes.usage: For runtime use, copy entries into an example's taint_config.json under the "taint" array. fn_name must match the demangled Rust symbol; return_type and parameter_type are checked by PointerAnalysis::isTaintedFunction (PointerAnalysis.cpp:1892).
_schema_notes.match_rule: demangled(callee) == fn_name AND returnType matches AND parameter_type.size() <= callee.arg_size()
_schema_notes.self_convention: For methods, parameter_type[0] is "sret" when present (see sret_convention below), followed by the receiver (&self / &mut self / self), matching the convention used in rust_input_functions.json for Tabby's chat/chat_stream.
_schema_notes.sret_convention: "sret" is prepended to parameter_type for every llm-api-chat entry whose return_type is Result<T, E> -- RUPTA's PAG models the indirect struct-return slot as a synthetic leading argument, since every response/error type catalogued here is multi-field and passed via a caller-allocated out-pointer rather than in registers. Shifts every real argument's position by one -- this is what request_index/prompt_arg_index below are indexed against.
_schema_notes.category_values: llm-api-prompt (building/assembling the request that will be sent -- message/content builders, request builders) | llm-api-chat (the outbound call that actually sends the assembled request to the LLM service). Optional per-entry field; entries without it predate this split and should be treated as llm-api-chat (they're all the outbound-call kind).
_schema_notes.request_index: llm-api-chat entries only: 0-based index into parameter_type of the argument that carries the assembled outbound request (or, for a builder-consuming call like `.execute(self)`, the index of `self` itself). This is the taint sink STPA should treat as "sent to the LLM".
_schema_notes.prompt_arg_index_and_role: llm-api-prompt entries only, and only on methods that actually take prompt/message content (not on plain field setters like `.model()` or on `.build()`, which finalizes already-accumulated state rather than taking new content): prompt_arg_index is the 0-based parameter_type index of the content-bearing argument; prompt_role classifies whose content it is -- "user" | "system" | "assistant" for a builder that constructs exactly one role's message, "mixed" for one that takes a whole collection of messages that could span roles (e.g. a Vec<ChatCompletionRequestMessage> batched from more than one place in the caller).
_schema_notes.async_sret_caveat: Every llm-api-chat entry here is an `async fn` (or a plain fn returning `impl Future`). Two real ABI shapes were confirmed by compiling against actual crates under rustc 1.86.0/LLVM 19.1.7 (2026-08 verification pass), and neither matches the sret_convention's stated rationale literally: (1) most entries (async-openai, ollama-rs, clust, misanthropic, genai, gemini-rust, rig-core) DO get a leading sret slot, but the sret'd value at the call site is the compiler-generated coroutine/future state-machine struct, not literally the Result<T,E> -- the Result only materializes later, as that future's Output, once something actually polls/awaits it. request_index/prompt_arg_index positions are unaffected (the real arguments still shift by one for the same structural reason), so the convention's *mechanics* hold even though its stated *reason* ("every response/error type is multi-field and passed via a caller-allocated out-pointer") is technically imprecise for async entries. (2) A plain (non-async_trait, non-async-fn) fn that returns `impl Future<...>` directly -- e.g. reqwest::RequestBuilder::send, or a trait method boxed via #[async_trait] like llm_chain::traits::Executor::execute -- gets NO sret at all when the returned future type is small enough to fit in registers (reqwest: 16 bytes, {i64,ptr}) or is itself a pointer-sized fat pointer (#[async_trait]'s Pin<Box<dyn Future+Send>>, {ptr,ptr}). Both of those entries were corrected to drop the leading "sret" and shift request_index down by one. Bottom line: don't assume sret from return_type alone for a new entry -- confirm against real IR, since the ABI depends on how the async fn is implemented (native async fn vs #[async_trait] vs plain fn returning impl Future), not just what it eventually returns.

rig-core.verified_via: llvm-ir:rustc-1.86.0+llvm-19.1.7 (rig-core 0.16.0 — latest verifiable under this pipeline's toolchain; rig-core 0.17.1 through the latest published 0.41.0 all fail to compile under rustc 1.86.0/LLVM19 due to let-chains, a hard MSRV wall unrelated to this dataset) — corrects the prior fn_name `rig::completion::Prompt::prompt`: missing the `request` module segment (`rig::completion::Prompt` still resolves via glob re-export, but the canonical/mangled-against path is `rig::completion::request::Prompt`). Real IR (monomorphized to Agent<M>): `define void @"...rig..agent..completion..Agent$LT$M$GT$...as...rig..completion..request..Prompt...6prompt..."(ptr sret([176 x i8]) align 8 %_0, ptr align 8 %self, ptr align 1 %prompt.0, i64 %prompt.1)` — confirms sret + &self + &str (2-word fat pointer) shape, request_index 2. Note: the sret'd value at this call site is actually the async PromptRequest builder/future object (176 bytes), not an immediate Result -- Result<String,PromptError> is the eventual Output once that future is driven, same async-deferred pattern as async_openai::chat::Chat::create in this file. Also note: as of rig-core 0.41.0 the crate split into a portable rig-core (contracts only) + rig-agent (classic runtime including Prompt/Agent), unified under a `rig` facade crate -- `Prompt` no longer lives in `rig-core` itself in the latest release, though the path catalogued here (pre-split) remains valid for the version range this was verified against.
rig-core.taint_role: provider-agnostic entry point; rig-core is a multi-provider framework (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Cohere, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Ollama, and more) built on the same CompletionModel trait, so this single signature covers call sites regardless of which provider client backs the Agent

rig-core.verified_via: llvm-ir:rustc-1.86.0+llvm-19.1.7 (rig-core 0.16.0 — same MSRV-wall caveat as Prompt::prompt above) — corrects the prior fn_name `rig::completion::CompletionModel::completion`: missing the `request` module segment, same as Prompt::prompt. Real IR (monomorphized to openai's ResponsesCompletionModel): `define void @"...rig..providers..openai..responses_api..ResponsesCompletionModel...as...rig..completion..request..CompletionModel...10completion..."(ptr sret([1456 x i8]) align 8 %_0, ptr align 8 %self, ptr align 8 %request)` — confirms sret + &self + CompletionRequest (passed indirectly despite being logically by-value, since it's large) shape, request_index 2. Same async-deferred sret caveat as Prompt::prompt above -- confirmed the real eventual Result<CompletionResponse<...>,...> (608 bytes) only appears after wrapping the call in futures::executor::block_on.
rig-core.taint_role: lower-level trait method implemented per-provider (rig::providers::anthropic, ::openai, ::gemini, etc.); catches direct completion-model usage bypassing the Agent/Prompt wrapper

anthropic-sdk.verified_via: llvm-ir:rustc-1.86.0+llvm-19.1.7 (anthropic-sdk 0.1.5) — corrects the prior guess of error type `AnthropicError`: no such type exists in the crate; it uses `anyhow::Result` throughout (`use anyhow::{anyhow, Context, Result}` in lib.rs). anthropic-sdk.taint_role: builder-entry; the actual black-box call is `.execute()`, reached only after `.build()?` on the request builder chain. request_index points at `self` (the built Request) -- that's the assembled outbound payload here, not the callback.

llvm-ir:rustc-1.88.0+llvm-20.1.5 (misanthropic 1.0.0-alpha.16) — corrects the prior guess of return type `ResponseStream`: the real re-exported type is literally named `Stream` (`pub use stream::Stream;`). llm-chain.verified_via: llvm-ir:rustc-1.86.0+llvm-19.1.7 (llm-chain 0.13.0, llm-chain-openai 0.13.0) — corrects the prior guess of an sret-prefixed 4-slot signature: real IR (monomorphized to the llm-chain-openai backend) shows `#[async_trait]` boxing returns a register-pair fat pointer `{ptr,ptr}` (Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Output, ExecutorError>> + Send>>), not an indirect sret struct-return — the sret_convention only applies when the *immediate* return type is Result<T,E>, which it isn't here. Real declare: `declare { ptr, ptr } @"_ZN93_$LT$llm_chain_openai..chatgpt..executor..Executor$u20$as$u20$llm_chain..traits..Executor$GT$7execute..."(ptr align 8, ptr align 8, ptr align 8)` — 3 real params (self=0, options=1, prompt=2), no leading sret slot.
llm-chain.taint_role: single-step black-box entry point; per-backend executors (llm-chain-openai, llm-chain-llama, etc.) all implement this trait method

llm-chain.verified_via: llvm-ir:rustc-1.86.0+llvm-19.1.7 (llm-chain 0.13.0, llm-chain-openai 0.13.0) — real IR confirms exactly: `define void @_ZN9llm_chain6chains10sequential5Chain3run17h873a73b8e7e580dcE(ptr sret([368 x i8]) align 8 %_0, ptr align 8 %self, ptr align 8 %parameters, ptr align 8 %executor)`; this one IS a plain (non-async_trait) generic async fn, so it keeps the ordinary sret ABI unlike Executor::execute above.
llm-chain.taint_role: request_index points at `Parameters` (the template-fill values that become the outbound prompt), not `&Executor` (just the backend reference)

raw-http-reqwest.verified_via: llvm-ir:rustc-1.86.0+llvm-19.1.7 (reqwest 0.13.4) — corrects the prior guess of an sret-prefixed 2-slot signature: `send()` itself isn't an `async fn`, it's a plain fn returning `impl Future<...>` directly, and that concrete future type is only 16 bytes, so it's returned in two registers (`{i64, ptr}`) with no indirect sret slot at all. Real IR: `declare { i64, ptr } @_ZN7reqwest10async_impl7request14RequestBuilder4send(ptr align 8)` -- only `self`, at index 0. `Result<Response, Error>` is what the *awaited* future yields, not send()'s own return type, so the dataset's blanket sret_convention (applies whenever return_type is Result<T,E>) doesn't hold for this entry -- real signature has to be checked case by case for plain fns returning `impl Future`.
raw-http-reqwest.taint_role: catch-all for LPAs that call provider HTTP APIs directly without an SDK; narrower match should be applied via URL/host predicate once we add that capability to STPA. request_index points at `self` (the built HTTP request) -- there's no separate request-struct argument for a raw reqwest call.

raw-http-reqwest.verified_via: llvm-ir:rustc-1.86.0+llvm-19.1.7 (reqwest 0.13.4) — confirmed as-is: `declare void @...blocking...RequestBuilder4send(ptr sret([176 x i8]) align 8, ptr align 8)`, sret=0, self=1. Unlike the async variant above, the blocking send() really does return Result<Response,Error> directly (176 bytes, indirect via sret), so the sret_convention holds here.
raw-http-reqwest.taint_role: blocking (sync) counterpart to reqwest::RequestBuilder::send; same catch-all role for LPAs using the blocking client
